study.title: The altered intrinsic functional connectivity after acupuncture at shenmen (HT7) in acute sleep deprivation
study.study_design: Within-subject repeated measures; all subjects underwent resting-state fMRI during rested wakefulness (RW) state and after 24 h of total sleep deprivation; the scan after 24 h of total SD included two resting-state fMRI sessions before and after needling at Shenmen (HT7)
study.population: Healthy subjects studying in college, aged 20-30 years (25.20 ± 2.20 years) with an education duration of 18.10 ± 2.45 years
study.disease_condition: Acute sleep deprivation (24 h total SD)
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) had no symptoms associated with sleep disorders and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index score < 5; (2) normal sleep patterns and not extreme morning or evening types according to Horne-Ostberg Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire; (3) right-handed; (4) no history of neurologic or psychiatric disorders; (5) no history of trauma stimuli for the latest 1 year; (6) no addiction of coffee, smoking, and alcohol; (7) no MRI contraindications

arms.arm_label_exact: Healthy subjects with regular sleep (within-subject, all conditions)

conditions.timepoint_exact: Beginning of study (8:00 am on day 1, before sleep deprivation)
conditions.scan_context: 490-s resting-state fMRI scan; subjects eyes closed, awake, at rest

conditions.condition_label_exact: After 24 h of total SD, before acupuncture at HT7
conditions.timepoint_exact: After 24 h of total sleep deprivation, after 7:00 am on day 2, before acupuncture
conditions.scan_context: 490-s resting-state fMRI scan; subjects eyes closed, awake, at rest

conditions.condition_label_exact: After 24 h of total SD, after acupuncture at HT7
conditions.timepoint_exact: After 24 h of total sleep deprivation and after 60-s acupuncture manipulation at HT7, day 2
conditions.scan_context: 490-s resting-state fMRI scan (without manipulation); subjects eyes closed, awake, at rest

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: located on the palmar ulnar end of the transverse crease of the wrist and on the radial aspect of the tendon of the ulnar flexor
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.5 mm in diameter and 40 mm in length
interventions.manipulation_exact: rotating the needle clockwise and counterclockwise at 1 Hz with even reinforcing and reducing manipulation for 60 s
interventions.session_duration_exact: 60-s acupuncture manipulation followed by 490-s resting-state scan
interventions.treatment_period_exact: Single session on day 2 after 24 h SD
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: the same two licensed and skilled acupuncturists
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: HT7 (Shenmen) is one of the most frequently used acupoints in improving sleep quality and cognitive impairments; recent clinical studies have revealed that acupuncture at HT7 had a beneficial effect on sleep disorders among Chinese people

sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: The paper does not explicitly report deqi sensation measurement or outcomes. Deqi was not formally assessed or reported.

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture control group was used. The authors acknowledge this limitation explicitly: 'without a control group of SD subjects with sham acupuncture treatment, we could not precisely quantify the effect of acupuncture on large-scale brain network FC.'
Deqi sensation was not formally measured or reported. No deqi assessment instrument was described or administered.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported.
Adverse events were not reported or discussed.
No cognitive or behavioral outcome measures were formally collected as primary outcomes. PSQI was used only as an inclusion criterion.
No PMID was reported in the document; only DOI is available.

Table 4 reports 'VAN-SMN' and 'SMN-VAN' as separate rows with the same t-value (-2.18) and p-value (0.04) for SD > RW comparisons. These appear to refer to the same network pair reported twice (once as VAN-SMN, once as SMN-VAN). Extracted as two separate entries to preserve the paper's exact table content.

The paper states 'SD > RW' for Table 4 rows with increased FC, but the t-values for decreased FC are negative (e.g., -2.18), indicating VAN-SMN and SMN-VAN are decreased in SD relative to RW. The table header 'SD > RW' is used for the entire block including both increased and decreased. Contrasts were separated per direction as reported.

The paper uses 'SMN-DAN' (t=2.15, p=0.04) in Table 4 under 'SD > RW' indicating increased FC, while the abstract and results text state 'increased between-network FC in DAN-VAN, DAN-SMN'. The edge DAN-SMN in the text corresponds to SMN-DAN in Table 4 (same pair). Extracted with the table label.

The paper reports 'depth_mm_numeric' as a range (20-30 mm). The numeric value entered (25) is an inferred midpoint and should not be treated as a precise reported value. The exact reported range is '20-30 mm'.

Figures 2, 3, 4, and 5 contain brain maps with affected edges and nodes, but individual region names and coordinates are not reported in the text or tables. Only network-level edge counts are tabulated. No coordinate tables exist in this paper.
Smoothing kernel size was not reported in the methods.
Global signal regression use was not explicitly reported.

The paper does not report the number of subjects who were excluded due to falling asleep during scanning, or whether any subjects were excluded post-hoc. The final analyzed N appears to be all 30 enrolled.
The paper states 'depth_mm_numeric' as inferred from the midpoint of the stated range. The exact wording is 'to a depth of 20-30 mm'.

The study is a within-subject design with no randomization reported. All 30 subjects completed all three conditions (RW, SD before acupuncture, SD after acupuncture). There is no parallel-group comparison.
